newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Apr palm oil output up 6.6 pct-Ivan Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Apr palm oil output up 6.6 pct-Ivan Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in April was estimated to have risen by 6.6 percent to 728,000 tonnes over March, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Wednesday.

Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of April at 695,000 tonnes, unchanged from his previous estimate. This compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 689,633 tonnes at end-March.
Wong in his previous report estimated exports in April at 610,000 tonnes against 565,219 tonnes in March.
Wong said for the first four months this year, production has expanded 10.6 percent to 2.49 million tonnes.
The growth is expected to slow down to around three percent in the next eight months, he said in a report.
Wong said indications of continuing keen competition from Indonesia in the export market may result in a modest rise in palm oil stocks in May and June.
In the first six months of the year, production was expected to trail offtake by 70,000 tonnes, Wong said.
Palm oil exports are projected to grow to 7.39 million tonnes in 1997 from 7.21 million last year.
The modest increase as compared to 700,000 tonnes recorded in 1996 reflected mainly a slowdown in production supplies as well as a marked reduction in crude palm oil imports, Wong said.
